name: ENCODE and SCREEN candidate cis-regulatory elements
maintainer: ENCODE Consortium (Stanford DCC); SCREEN (Weng lab, UMass)

version.value: Registry V4 cCREs (Nature 2026 citation); ENCODE portal queried 2026-10-25

scope: 20,450 released human experiments (e.g. TF ChIP-seq 3,502; DNase-seq 3,144; histone ChIP-seq 3,090; total RNA-seq 1,650; ATAC-seq 463); SCREEN Registry V4 lists 2,348,854 human cCREs in 1,888 cell types with per-class BED files.
mapping_methods: cCREs are genomic intervals; variants are intersected by coordinates (GRCh37 files are lifted down from GRCh38).

quantitative.summary: Element classes and signal tracks; not variant effects.

licence.name: No licence name found. SCREEN states that all SCREEN data is publicly available for download and asks users to cite Moore et al. (2026, Nature); ENCODE's own data-use page returned HTTP 403 to automated access and is unread.
licence.redistribution: Not confirmed; treat as use-with-citation and do not redistribute until the ENCODE data-use terms are read.

update_frequency: Registry versions every few years; portal continuous.
coverage_limitations: cCREs are predicted from biochemical marks and are not proof of regulatory function
known_omissions: Variant-to-function effects require MPRA/CRISPR data (see MaveDB) or predictors (Enformer)

reuse_decision.rationale: SCREEN already integrates ENCODE and partner data into a registry; use the class BED files (about 129 MB for non-overlapping classes) instead of parsing thousands of experiments.

status.notes: API and SCREEN download links resolved by rendering the downloads page.
